column12: JUDGEMENT on the choice of comparator. Vraylar holds an adjunctive MDD label (approved December 2022), the same setting as the RENEW trials, and the book carries its demand. Caplyta, which holds the same adjunctive-MDD label (November 2025), comes in at $9,940 per beneficiary in 2024 and supports the anchor. The case against it: Vraylar's Medicare spend is mostly schizophrenia and bipolar use, and Lilly may price an incretin at the class level instead: Mounjaro $7,084, Ozempic $6,642 per beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand). That price would be about 27% lower. Rexulti, the most-used adjunctive-MDD brand, is not in the book's demand table

column11: house convention: halving a CMS per-beneficiary figure lands at a median 96% of CMS's own negotiated net prices (retatrutide seed, backend/gross_to_net.py)

column11: Auvelity, CMS Part D (lookup.py demand Auvelity): 9,268 beneficiaries in 2023, 16,448 in 2024. Pool: 53.1mm Part D enrollees in 2024 (KFF, Key Facts About Medicare Part D Enrollment, Premiums, and Cost Sharing in 2024) x 17.54% of Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries with depressive disorders in 2022 (CMS Chronic Conditions Warehouse, Medicare chronic condition charts) = 9,313,740, with NO further treated-share factor, because the CCW flag is built from diagnosis claims and so already counts only beneficiaries seen for depression. New patients in 2024 = 16,448 - 9,268 x (1 - 0.648) = 13,186, over 9,313,740 - 9,268 = 9,304,472 = 0.1417%
column12: JUDGEMENT: a 1.0x multiple on Auvelity. Corrected by the second reader from 0.2325%. The researcher multiplied the CCW diagnosed share by the NSDUH 61.0% treated share. NSDUH's 61% is the share of people with an MDE in a household survey (diagnosed or not) who received treatment; the CCW 17.54% already counts only beneficiaries with a depression diagnosis on a claim, which is itself a health-professional contact. Applying 61% again double-counts the treatment filter and shrinks the Medicare pool 1.64x, inflating the rate 1.64x. The engine divides by prevalence x eligible_pct = the treated US MDE pool, and its Medicare counterpart is the claims-diagnosed pool, not 61% of it. Remaining caveats: CCW 'depressive disorders' is broader than MDD (dysthymia, other depressive disorders), which biases this rate down; the CCW share is fee-for-service only but is applied to all Part D enrollees including MA-PD; 2024 is Auvelity's second full year and not its peak (FY2025 net sales $507.1mm, up 74%, Axsome 8-K 23 Feb 2026); and Auvelity's Medicare rate is applied to an all-payer US pool. Arithmetic unchanged otherwise: the 64.8% stop rate is the asset field
